points.t: **Hypopigmented or red patches with reduced sensation**, thickened nerves, painless burns or ulcers, in someone from an endemic country.
*M. leprae* infects **Schwann cells and macrophages**; immunity sets the tuberculoid–lepromatous position.
Refer to the **UK leprosy service** (Hospital for Tropical Diseases); WHO MDT; address stigma; protect numb hands and feet.
**Type 1 (reversal) reactions** and **ENL**: nerve pain, weakness or painful nodules need urgent specialist steroids.

cause.lead: Slow bacillus, cool sites, immune spectrum.
points: Obligate intracellular AFB, divides every **12–14 days**; prefers cool sites (skin, nerves, nose, earlobes, testes); incubation ~5 years.
Spread by **droplets from untreated MB patients** after prolonged household contact; ~95% resistant; **non-infectious within days of MDT**.
**Tuberculoid** (strong Th1): few defined lesions, early nerve damage. **Lepromatous** (weak CMI): many lesions, many bacilli.
WHO: **PB** 1–5 lesions, smear −; **MB** > 5 lesions or smear +.
UK: ~10–15 cases a year, all acquired abroad; statutorily notifiable.

features.lead: WHO cardinal signs: ≥ 1 makes the diagnosis.
points: **Definite loss of sensation in a pale or reddish patch.**
**Thickened peripheral nerve** with sensory loss and / or weakness.
**AFB on slit-skin smear.**
TT: 1–3 sharply defined **dry, hairless, anaesthetic** plaques. BB: ‘Swiss-cheese’ annular lesions. LL: diffuse infiltration, nodules, **earlobe thickening**, leonine facies.
Painless trophic ulcers and burns from sensory loss.

visuals.caption: Test every pale patch for sensation with a wisp of cotton wool (and warm / cold, monofilament). A numb, dry, hairless patch is leprosy until proven otherwise.
visuals.alt: Gloved hand touching a pale forearm patch with cotton wool

points: **Consultant Advisor in Leprosy before** smears or biopsies (UKHSA).
Sensory testing of lesions, **nerve palpation**, voluntary muscle test.
**Slit-skin smear** (earlobes, forehead, lesions: BI); deep biopsy from the active edge (Fite stain).

cards.name: Erythema nodosum (vs ENL)
cards.clue: Tender shin nodules; strep, sarcoid, IBD, drugs.

manage.lead: Primary care: suspect, refer, support adherence, spot reactions and drug effects.

points: Refer every suspected case to a **national leprosy centre** (e.g. HTD, UCLH).
Notify to UKHSA (confidential); contacts via CCDC / UKHSA.
Address **stigma**; patients are non-infectious soon after MDT starts.
**PB 6 months; MB 12 months.**

rx.dose: 300 mg once a month (supervised) + 50 mg daily

points: **Continue MDT.** Type 1: prednisolone (~40 mg/day tapered over 3–6 months) + splint.
ENL: NSAIDs if mild; prednisolone (~40–60 mg/day) if moderate–severe; clofazimine high-dose; **thalidomide** under a Pregnancy Prevention Programme.
**Rifampicin**: enzyme induction (contraception → IUD / condoms per FSRH; warfarin, DOACs, ARVs, azoles, ciclosporin, methadone, steroids); orange urine and tears.
**Dapsone**: haemolysis, methaemoglobinaemia, **hypersensitivity syndrome** in first 4–6 weeks; FBC, LFT.
**Clofazimine**: red-brown to grey-black skin discolouration.

limits.t: Daily self-examination of numb hands, feet and eyes; protective footwear.

items.t: Reaction: new **nerve pain or weakness**, ENL with fever, **new foot drop or claw hand**.
Eye pain, redness, reduced vision or can’t close the eye: **same-day ophthalmology**.
Any suspected leprosy: Consultant Advisor / national leprosy centre.

pearls.t: A **numb** pale patch is leprosy until proven otherwise; ordinary pale patches feel normal.
Reactions are nerve emergencies, not a reason to stop MDT.
Rifampicin, even monthly, matters for contraception around the dose day.
Stigma is a major barrier: confidential, non-judgemental care.

quiz.a: Anaesthetic patch, thickened nerve with loss, AFB on slit-skin smear.
Type 1 reaction: urgent specialist (steroids); continue MDT.
